questions.questionText: What does LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network, which connects devices within a limited area like a home, office, or building.

questions.questionText: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for routing packets between different networks using IP addresses.

questions.questionText: What is the default port number for HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTP uses port 80 by default. HTTPS uses port 443.

questions.questionText: Which protocol is used to retrieve email from a server?
questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is used to retrieve email from a mail server.

questions.questionText: What is the full form of TCP?
questions.explanation: TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol, which provides reliable, ordered delivery of data.

questions.questionText: Which device is used to connect multiple networks together?
questions.explanation: A Router connects multiple networks together and routes packets between them based on IP addresses.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum length of a CAT5 Ethernet cable?
questions.explanation: The maximum length of a CAT5 Ethernet cable is 100 meters (328 feet).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a Class B IP address?
questions.explanation: Class B IP addresses range from 128.0.0.0 to 191.255.255.255. So 172.16.0.1 is a Class B address.

questions.questionText: What does DNS stand for?
questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System, which translates domain names to IP addresses.

questions.questionText: Which protocol uses port 443?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) uses port 443 by default for encrypted web traffic.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of ARP?
options: To map IP addresses to MAC addresses
To map MAC addresses to IP addresses
questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network.

questions.questionText: Which topology has a single central hub or switch?
questions.explanation: In Star Topology, all devices are connected to a central hub or switch.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of the Transport Layer?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer provides end-to-end communication services, including segmentation, flow control, and error recovery.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a routing protocol?
questions.explanation: TCP is a transport layer protocol, not a routing protocol. OSPF, BGP, and RIP are routing protocols.

questions.questionText: What is the subnet mask for a /24 network?
questions.explanation: A /24 network has 24 bits for the network portion, so the subnet mask is 255.255.255.0.

questions.questionText: Which layer of the OSI model handles encryption and decryption?
questions.explanation: The Presentation Layer (Layer 6) handles data translation, encryption, and decryption.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of NAT?
options: To translate private IP addresses to public IP addresses
questions.explanation: NAT (Network Address Translation) translates private IP addresses to public IP addresses for internet access.

questions.questionText: Which protocol is connectionless?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery of data.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of hosts in a /26 network?
questions.explanation: A /26 network has 6 host bits (32-26=6), so it supports 2^6 - 2 = 62 usable host addresses.

questions.questionText: Which device operates at Layer 2 of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: A Switch operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) and uses MAC addresses to forward frames.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of DHCP?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses and network configuration to devices.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a private IP address range?
questions.explanation: 192.168.x.x is one of the private IP address ranges (RFC 1918).

questions.questionText: What does ICMP stand for?
questions.explanation: ICMP stands for Internet Control Message Protocol, used for diagnostic and error reporting (e.g., ping).

questions.questionText: Which topology has all devices connected to each other?
questions.explanation: In Mesh Topology, every device is connected to every other device, providing multiple paths for data.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of SSL/TLS?
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) encrypts data transmitted between client and server.

questions.questionText: Which protocol is used for sending email?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending email messages.

questions.questionText: What is the broadcast address for the network 192.168.1.0/24?
questions.explanation: The broadcast address has all host bits set to 1, so for 192.168.1.0/24 it is 192.168.1.255.

questions.questionText: Which layer of the OSI model is closest to the end user?
questions.explanation: The Application Layer (Layer 7) is closest to the end user and provides network services directly to applications.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between a hub and a switch?
options: A hub is faster than a switch
A switch sends data only to the intended recipient, a hub broadcasts to all ports
A hub is Layer 2 device, a switch is Layer 1 device
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: A switch intelligently forwards data only to the destination port using MAC addresses, while a hub broadcasts to all ports.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a firewall?
options: To monitor and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic
questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predefined security rules.

questions.questionText: Which class of IP address has the default subnet mask 255.255.0.0?
questions.explanation: Class B IP addresses have a default subnet mask of 255.255.0.0 (/16).
